events.title: Internet Explorer 6.0 released
events.summary: [Microsoft] released [Internet Explorer] 6.0 on August 27, 2001 — the version that dominated the web for years and became infamous among developers.
events.about: [IE] 6 shipped with Windows XP and became the browser most of the world used — and most sites were built for. Its slow update cycle, security holes, and [CSS] quirks forced an entire industry of hacks, conditional comments, and later campaigns like "IE6 must die."

narrative.whyChosen: [IE] 6's long reign shaped web development pain points and motivated [Firefox] and [Chrome].
narrative.whyImportant: Market dominance plus stagnation made cross-browser compatibility a full-time job for a decade.
narrative.problemSolved: [Microsoft] bundled a capable-enough browser with XP, giving users immediate web access on new PCs.

events.title: Eric Schmidt named Google CEO
events.summary: Google hired Eric Schmidt as CEO in August 2001, pairing adult supervision with founders Page and Brin during hypergrowth.
events.about: Schmidt's era scaled Google's ad business, [IPO], and [Android] [acquisition] — turning a search startup into a diversified platform company. The 'adult supervision' model influenced how VC-backed startups structure founder/CEO roles.

narrative.whyChosen: Schmidt guided Google from startup to public platform giant.
narrative.whyImportant: He professionalized operations while founders kept product vision.
narrative.problemSolved: Young technical founders needed experienced leadership for scaling and [IPO] readiness.
